pharm: Long-acting dopamine D2-receptor agonist; inhibits prolactin secretion
quick: Suppresses lactation; avoid in nursing mothers
Caution in severe impairment; reduce dose
summary: Cabergoline is a long-acting oral dopamine D2-agonist (ergot derivative) used to treat hyperprolactinemic disorders, either idiopathic or due to pituitary adenomas. Its very long half-life allows convenient twice-weekly dosing. Treatment starts at 0.25 mg twice a week and is titrated to serum prolactin, to a maximum of 1 mg twice weekly. Cardiac valve assessment is advised because of ergot-related fibrosis risk.

dosage.n: Increase by 0.25 mg twice weekly no faster than every 4 weeks

dosage.d: Up to 1 mg twice a week
dosage.n: Titrate to serum prolactin; do not exceed 1 mg twice weekly

admin: Take twice weekly, with or without food
Perform cardiovascular evaluation and consider echocardiography before starting
Titrate dose no more often than every 4 weeks
Monitor serum prolactin to guide dosing
Discontinuation often attempted after prolactin normalized for 6 months
moa: Potent, long-acting dopamine D2-receptor agonist that directly inhibits prolactin secretion from pituitary lactotrophs.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to cabergoline or any ergot derivative
History of pulmonary, pericardial or retroperitoneal fibrotic disorders
History of cardiac valvulopathy (anatomical evidence of valve damage)

preg: Limited data; usually discontinue once pregnancy is recognized unless medically necessary. Animal data showed no teratogenicity at therapeutic exposures.
lact: Cabergoline inhibits/suppresses lactation; not recommended in women intending to breastfeed.
renal: No specific dose adjustment established; pharmacokinetics not significantly altered in renal impairment.
hepatic: Increased exposure in severe hepatic impairment; use lower doses and caution.

major: Dopamine antagonists (phenothiazines, butyrophenones, metoclopramide) — reduce cabergoline efficacy
Other ergot alkaloids — additive fibrotic/vasospastic risk
moderate: Strong P-glycoprotein/CYP modulators — theoretical exposure changes
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; alcohol may worsen dizziness and orthostatic hypotension.

monitoring: Echocardiography for valvular disease (baseline and periodically)
Blood pressure, especially orthostatic, on initiation
counsel: Take twice a week exactly as directed
Avoid driving if drowsy; sudden sleep onset can occur
Report shortness of breath, persistent cough, or leg/abdominal swelling
Tell your doctor about new gambling, shopping or sexual urges
Inform your doctor if you become pregnant
pearls: Twice-weekly dosing thanks to very long half-life
More effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine for prolactinomas
Ergot derivative — obtain echocardiography and assess for valve disease before/during therapy
Can cause impulse-control disorders; ask specifically at follow-up
Higher fibrosis risk relates to high cumulative doses used in Parkinson disease, not the low prolactin doses
missed: Take as soon as remembered unless near the next scheduled dose; do not double up. Resume the twice-weekly schedule.
overdose: Symptoms reflect dopaminergic overstimulation: hypotension, nasal congestion, nausea, hallucinations. Provide supportive care, maintain blood pressure; dopamine antagonists may help if needed.
